title: 1960 AHSME Problem 35
statement: From point \(P\) outside a circle, with a circumference of \(10\) units, a tangent is drawn. Also from \(P\) a secant is drawn dividing the circle into unequal arcs with lengths \(m\) and \(n.\) It is found that \(t,\) the length of the tangent, is the mean proportional between \(m\) and \(n.\) If \(m\) and \(t\) are integers, then \(t\) may have the following number of values:

solutions.text:
The arc lengths satisfy \(m+n=10,\) while the mean-proportional condition gives \[ t^2=mn=m(10-m). \] For integral \(m\) from \(1\) through \(9,\) the possible products, up to symmetry, are \(9,\) \(16,\) \(21,\) \(24,\) and \(25.\) The last comes from equal arcs \(m=n=5\) and is excluded. The remaining squares give \(t=3\) and \(t=4,\) two values.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Test the integer values \(m=1,2,\ldots,9,\) excluding equal arcs
